summary:
AtlasX is an interactive Martian exploration and mission-planning platform developed to support the study of Mars and the challenges of future human exploration. It integrates 3D planetary visualization, scientific surface mapping, astronaut EVA (Extravehicular Activity) calculations, meteorological hazard assessment and astronomical telemetry into a unified interface.

The platform enables users to explore major Martian geographical features, analyse elevation and infrared maps, assess astronaut metabolic energy expenditure and oxygen consumption, and evaluate mission safety under changing dust and temperature conditions. It also incorporates Mars time calculations, solar positioning data and planetary surface imagery to support informed exploration planning.

AtlasX addresses the challenge by transforming diverse planetary datasets and mission-related calculations into an accessible, interactive decision-support environment. By combining geographical, environmental and human-safety factors, it helps users understand the complexity of operating on Mars and the importance of resource management, route planning and astronaut safety.

Its significance lies in bringing multiple aspects of Martian exploration together in one platform, supporting scientific learning, mission research and the development of safer strategies for future human exploration of Mars.
details:
Project Details – AtlasX

Planetary Surface Intelligence & Mission Planning Platform

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

AtlasX is an interactive Martian exploration and mission-planning platform designed to bring multiple aspects of Mars exploration into a unified digital environment. It combines 3D planetary visualization, scientific surface mapping, astronaut EVA (Extravehicular Activity) calculations, environmental hazard assessment and astronomical telemetry.

Users can explore the Martian surface through an interactive 3D globe, examine geographical features and scientific mapping layers, and investigate environmental conditions. The EVA module estimates astronaut metabolic energy expenditure, oxygen consumption and Point of No Return constraints. The environmental assessment module considers dust visibility and temperature-related risks. The platform also provides Mars-specific time and astronomical information, including Mars Sol Date, Mars Coordinated Time, solar longitude, heliocentric distance and solar irradiance.

By integrating these capabilities, AtlasX provides a connected environment for understanding the geographical, environmental and human factors involved in future Martian missions.

2. What are the benefits?

  • Integrated exploration: Combines planetary mapping, environmental assessment and mission-related calculations in one platform.
  • Better understanding of Mars: Makes complex scientific datasets easier to explore and interpret.
  • Astronaut safety awareness: Helps evaluate oxygen requirements, energy expenditure and EVA return constraints.
  • Environmental awareness: Highlights the influence of dust and temperature on surface operations.
  • Educational value: Provides an interactive way for students, researchers and space enthusiasts to understand Martian exploration.

3. What is the intended impact?

The primary objective of AtlasX is to make Martian exploration data more accessible and useful for preliminary mission planning and scientific learning. It aims to encourage a more integrated understanding of planetary geography, environmental conditions and human operational limitations.

In the long term, AtlasX could serve as an educational and research-support platform for exploring mission scenarios, understanding operational challenges and developing awareness of the requirements for future human exploration of Mars. It is intended as a decision-support concept rather than a replacement for validated mission-control or life-support systems.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

AtlasX was developed using modern web technologies and 3D visualization frameworks.

  • Frontend: React 18
  • Programming languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML and CSS
  • Build tool: Vite 5
  • 3D visualization: Three.js
  • Mapping: Leaflet
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS
  • Icons: Lucide React
  • Scientific data and mapping: MOLA elevation data, Viking imagery and THEMIS infrared data, as documented in the project.

The application is designed as a software-based platform and does not require dedicated physical hardware for its core functionality.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The main innovation of AtlasX is its integration of several traditionally separate aspects of planetary exploration into a single interactive platform. Instead of treating Mars mapping, astronaut resource calculations, environmental hazards and astronomical information as independent subjects, AtlasX connects them through a unified exploration workflow.

Its combination of 3D planetary visualization, EVA resource estimation, environmental assessment and Mars-specific telemetry provides a distinctive way to understand the relationship between the Martian environment and human mission requirements.

The project also focuses on presenting complex scientific information through an accessible and modern interface, making planetary exploration more engaging and understandable.

6. What factors did the team consider?

During the development of AtlasX, the following factors were considered:

  • Scientific relevance: Using appropriate planetary datasets and Mars-specific parameters.
  • Astronaut safety: Considering oxygen consumption, metabolic expenditure and return limitations.
  • Environmental challenges: Recognizing dust conditions and extreme temperatures.
  • Usability: Designing an intuitive interface for exploring complex scientific information.
  • Performance: Maintaining responsive 3D visualization and smooth application navigation.
  • Integration: Bringing different scientific and mission-planning modules into one environment.
  • Scalability: Allowing opportunities to incorporate additional datasets, analytical tools and mission-planning capabilities in the future.

Conclusion

AtlasX aims to transform the way people explore and understand Mars by connecting planetary science, environmental awareness and human mission requirements in one interactive platform. By making complex information more accessible and bringing multiple mission perspectives together, it contributes to a broader understanding of the challenges and possibilities of future human exploration of Mars.
